_doc: The ONE shipping truth for Forge (ORG-03/04). Every source path of this repository (git tracked + untracked-not-ignored; paths relative to the project root) gets exactly one class from the ordered `rules` list — LAST MATCH WINS, like .gitignore, so broad globs come first and explicit overrides after. Glob syntax: `**` any depth (`**/` also zero folders), `*` and `?` never cross `/`, `{a,b}` alternatives. A catch-all (`**`, `.claude/**`, ...) is refused by the checker. Classes: ship-sync = copied into every Forge project by forge-sync and kept fresh (channels must include sync); seed-only = created in a project when absent, never overwritten (owner state with a template default); ship-release-only = in the public release tree and the template, never file-synced (settings.json reaches projects through forge-settings-merge, `delivery: settings-merge`); installer-only = read by install.ps1/install.sh from the release tree; global-install = installed into ~/.claude by the installer; per-project = each project's own data or runtime state, never shipped (a shipped file may point at it); local-only = exists only in this development tree, never leaves it; retired = gone on purpose, needs a `replacement`. channels: sync (forge-sync to projects), release (public tree / GitHub), plugin (plugins/forge), template (~/.claude/forge/template). A ship-sync/seed-only entry without the release channel needs a `release_excluded` reason. `ref_ok` lets shipped files point at a path that never reaches projects (with the reason); `ref_ignore` silences one exact from->ref pair. `known_gaps` lists genuine gaps whose fix is code in another work package: matching violations are WARNINGS (with that WP), everything else FAILS the enforced doctor check `ship_manifest`. Checker: .claude/forge-bin/forge-shipcheck.cjs (CLI --json, --no-known-gaps, --release-tree <dir>).
